title: Teaching children (Deuteronomy 6:7)
hookLine: teach them diligently, at home and on the way
tomorrow: teach a grandchild, says the Talmud, and it's as if what?

lines: IS GOD REAL? ONE SHOE ON.
cards: Kids ask the biggest questions at the worst moments: from the back seat, in the bath, halfway out the door with one shoe on. Why do people die? Is God real?
Where was I before I was born? Nobody schedules those. A verse in Deuteronomy seems to have known that already.

teach.h: AT HOME, ON THE WAY, AT BEDTIME.
teach.b: It's in the Shema, and the JPS translation reads: "and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up."
Look where the teaching happens. Not at a desk. At home, on a walk, at bedtime, at breakfast.
The teaching rides along with ordinary life.

teach.h: SHARP IN YOUR MOUTH: NO STAMMER.
teach.b: The Hebrew for teach them diligently is v'shinantam, and Rashi reads it this way: let the words be sharp in your mouth, so that when someone asks, you don't stammer, you answer. Short, clear, ready.
The Talmud, in Kiddushin, lists what a father owes his son, and it's practical: teach him Torah, teach him a trade, and some say, teach him to swim. Teaching for a whole life, not only for a test.
None of it requires a parent with every answer.

teach.h: WHAT WE SAY, WHAT I WONDER.
teach.b: Here's a sentence a parent could say at dinner: that's a big question; here's what our tradition says, here's what I still wonder, let's look it up together.

how: Deuteronomy 6:7 is part of the Shema, said morning and evening; Jewish parents teach at home through Shabbat and holidays, bedtime Shema and questions at the table, alongside Hebrew school or day school.

games.q: your niece asks at bedtime, 'is God real?' you're not sure what you think. what fits Deuteronomy 6:7 and Rashi?
o: say what the tradition says, what you wonder, and offer to look together.
change the subject; bedtime is for sleep, and teaching is for class.
tell her to save it for her Hebrew school teacher next week.
games.why: the verse puts teaching at bedtime, and Rashi wants a ready answer, not a stammer. honest and short counts.

practice: Choose one thing you know well enough to teach a child: a blessing, a story, how to tie a knot, how to say sorry. Say it out loud in one plain sentence, as if a kid had just asked from the back seat.
Then say it once more, shorter and sharper.

wordCard.voice: Teaching children: diligently, at home and on the way, at bedtime and at breakfast. Sharp in your mouth, ready when they ask.

orig.note: Hebrew: 'and you shall teach them diligently' (Deuteronomy 6:7); Rashi: let them be sharp in your mouth.

carryVoice: To carry: teach them diligently, on the way as much as at the table. That's six in home and family.
